logic_node.action: Consider wireless PA pressure monitoring by implanted hemodynamic monitor
logic_node.action_detail: In selected adult patients with NYHA class III HF and history of a HF hospitalization in the past year or elevated natriuretic peptide levels, on maximally tolerated stable doses of GDMT with optimal device therapy, the usefulness of wireless monitoring of PA pressure by an implanted hemodynamic monitor to reduce the risk of subsequent HF hospitalizations is uncertain.

source_text: In selected adult patients with NYHA class III HF and history of a HF hospitalization in the past year or elevated natriuretic peptide levels, on maximally tolerated stable doses of GDMT with optimal device therapy, the usefulness of wireless monitoring of PA pressure by an implanted hemodynamic monitor to reduce the risk of subsequent HF hospitalizations is uncertain.

logic_node.action: Assess cost-effectiveness of wireless PA pressure monitoring
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with NYHA class III HF with a HF hospitalization within the previous year, wireless monitoring of the PA pressure by an implanted hemodynamic monitor provides uncertain value. Cost-effectiveness analyses show increased survival and QALYs but also increased costs, with estimates ranging from high to intermediate value.

source_text: In patients with NYHA class III HF with a HF hospitalization within the previous year, wireless monitoring of the PA pressure by an implanted hemodynamic monitor provides uncertain value.

logic_node.action: Assess and document NYHA functional classification
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HF, assessment and documentation of NYHA functional classification are recommended to determine eligibility for treatments. NYHA class I: no limitations; class II: slight symptoms with ordinary activity; class III: symptoms with less than ordinary activity; class IV: symptoms at rest.

source_text: In patients with HF, assessment and documentation of NYHA functional classification are recommended to determine eligibility for treatments.

logic_node.action: Perform cardiopulmonary exercise testing for advanced therapy candidacy
logic_node.action_detail: In selected ambulatory patients with HF, cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) is recommended to determine appropriateness of advanced treatments such as LVAD and heart transplant.

source_text: In selected ambulatory patients with HF, cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) is recommended to determine appropriateness of advanced treatments (eg, LVAD, heart transplant).

logic_node.action: Perform CPET or 6-minute walk test to assess functional capacity
logic_node.action_detail: In ambulatory patients with HF, performing a cardiopulmonary exercise test (CPET) or 6-minute walk test is reasonable to assess functional capacity.

source_text: In ambulatory patients with HF, performing a CPET or 6-minute walk test is reasonable to assess functional capacity.

logic_node.action: Perform CPET to evaluate cause of unexplained dyspnea
logic_node.action_detail: In ambulatory patients with unexplained dyspnea, cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) is reasonable to evaluate the cause of dyspnea. CPET can help distinguish respiratory versus cardiac etiologies of dyspnea.

source_text: In ambulatory patients with unexplained dyspnea, CPET is reasonable to evaluate the cause of dyspnea.

logic_node.action: Consider heart transplant listing based on peak VO2
logic_node.action_detail: Peak VO2 <= 14 mL/kg/min is the cutoff to distinguish patients who may derive survival benefit from heart transplant. Patients with peak VO2 >14 mL/kg/min who were deferred had 1- and 2-year survival of 94% and 84%, respectively, similar to survival after heart transplant.

source_text: Patients with peak VO2 <=14 mL/kg/min were listed for transplant... the authors proposed peak VO2 <= 14 mL/kg/min as a cutoff to distinguish patients who may derive survival benefit from heart transplant.

logic_node.action: Consider heart transplant listing for patients on beta blockers based on adjusted peak VO2 cutoff
logic_node.action_detail: For patients on beta blockers, a peak VO2 <= 12 mL/kg/min has been suggested as a more appropriate cutoff to consider cardiac transplant listing, as patients tolerating beta blockers may have improved survival with an equivalent VO2 compared with patients who do not tolerate beta blockers.

source_text: For patients on beta blockers, a peak VO2 <=12 mL/kg/min has been suggested as a more appropriate cutoff to consider cardiac transplant listing.

logic_node.action: Identify high-risk HF patients based on 6-minute walk test distance
logic_node.action_detail: A 6-minute walk test distance <300 m roughly correlates to patients with NYHA class III to IV symptoms and is associated with worse 3-year survival free of heart transplant (62% versus 82% for those walking >= 300 m).

source_text: A cutoff of <300 m roughly correlates to patients with NYHA class III to IV symptoms and is associated with worse 3-year survival free of heart transplant (62% versus 82% for those walking >= 300 m).

logic_node.action: Use validated multivariable risk scores to estimate mortality risk
logic_node.action_detail: In ambulatory or hospitalized patients with HF, validated multivariable risk scores can be useful to estimate subsequent risk of mortality. Commonly used scores include the Seattle Heart Failure Model, Heart Failure Survival Score, and MAGGIC score for chronic HF; PARADIGM-HF and HF-ACTION for HFrEF; I-PRESERVE and TOPCAT for HFpEF; and ADHERE CART, AHA GWTG, EFFECT, and ESCAPE scores for acute decompensated HF.

source_text: In ambulatory or hospitalized patients with HF, validated multivariable risk scores can be useful to estimate subsequent risk of mortality.
